The pattern repeats: OpenCode refactors the instance bootstrap, ALS context propagation breaks, and plugins silently fail to register agents/MCPs. The root cause is the same — plugin async callbacks lose \Instance.current\ (ALS) across Effect/async boundaries. Our issue provides the exact code-level diagnosis and a suggested fix for the v1.14.32 occurrence.

You're right, the JSON storage path was stale — opencode moved to SQLite a while back (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` on the `latest` channel; `opencode db path` prints the exact location).

For the cut-off you pasted above, the equivalent of "what's actually in storage" is one query:

```bash
opencode db "SELECT json_extract(data, '$.text') AS text FROM part WHERE session_id = '<ses_id>' AND json_extract(data, '$.type') = 'text' ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1" --format json
```

Replace `<ses_id>` with the session you resumed (the value after `opencode -s `). That returns the raw `text` field from the most recent assistant text part — no schema spelunking, no `.db` to send.

If the stored text ends at the same spot the TUI shows (`...fn fetch_game(&self, game_id: &str`), the bug is in the stream→storage write path — chunks dropped before the part row is updated.

If the stored text continues past that spot, the bug is in the renderer — the parse/render layer cuts off deterministically on the same input.

The "stops for a second, then ends" detail is consistent with the renderer side: a worker (tree-sitter highlighter, inline-HTML parser) hitting a state it can't make progress on, then the stream completes and the TUI never gets a render trigger for the trailing tokens. The build-mode samples ending mid-`</invoke>` push the same direction because those are MarkdownRenderable parsing inline-HTML at chunk boundaries. But the storage check is what splits it cleanly.
